items.title: DECISION NEEDED: the rational-point hypothesis, and the blueprint describing an abandoned route.
DECIDED: etale-sheafify — no rational-point binder on the headline
Wire the headline to the infrastructure

commits.subject: chore(horizon): record the measured build baseline and file the two decisions for the owner
commits.summary:
I-0319 now carries the re-measured from-scratch build (43:15.98, 9.7 GB, 8,723 jobs green), the finding that the wall clock is critical-path bound rather than throughput bound, the per-file umbrella cost (16.6s/7GB vs 3.5s/2.0GB), and the correction that the 289 `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency` scopes match upstream practice and should be left alone.

A new `to human` issue states the two questions that outrank all mechanical work: whether to étale-sheafify the Picard functor (mathlib v4.31 does have the étale topology, so the rational-point binder is a design choice, not a platform limit), and whether to re-aim the 8,434-line Quot blueprint chapter at the Milne--Kollár route the tree actually committed to on 9 July.
